title: Proactive slate seeder and KV stabilizer for predictable Dedicated cold-start reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets still see a non-trivial fraction of cold-start requests during traffic ramps. Cold-starts are dominated by two phases: model weight load time and KV cache population. Existing warm-pool implementations focus on fully-resident weight snapshots, which reduces weight fetch latency but leaves KV priming and per-tenant prefix coverage under-provisioned, causing tail latency spikes and missed throughput guarantees for committed customers.

Proposal: Implement a two-part subsystem named 'Slate Seeder' (proactive, lightweight weight/layout seeding) and 'KV Stabilizer' (targeted KV prefix hydration and soft-lease stabilization) that work with autoscaler/fleet controls to deliver deterministic throughput for Dedicated tenants during onboarding and burst ramps. Slate Seeder will pre-stage minimal parameter shards and crucial attention+embedding kernels so instances can begin serving with reduced parameter transfer; KV Stabilizer will prewarm critical prefix sets and maintain a probabilistic cover set per tenant using background prioritized sweeps. Both components integrate with the admission controller and autoscaler to coordinate soft reservations and priority windows.

Key design differentiators vs previous work: slate-based minimal residency (small footprint snapshots) instead of full weight snapshotting; probabilistic prefix cover using reservoir sampling and LRU-lift heuristics (instead of naive full-key prefetch); close coupling with autoscaler so prewarming is elastic and budgeted to respect memory/throughput SLAs.

Trade-offs:
- Memory vs. Coverage: Slate Seeder reduces weight residency at the cost of slightly higher per-request compute until full weights stream in; KV Stabilizer trades memory for lower tail latency (we will tune cover size per tenant tier).
- Network vs. Local Compute: Staged streaming reduces peak network bursts but may add CPU contention during initial requests.
- Complexity vs. Predictability: Adds orchestration surface (leases, admission hooks) but yields clearer throughput guarantees for high-commit tenants.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Tail P95 latency for committed Dedicated tenants during 3x traffic ramp reduces by >=40% compared to baseline without seeding; 2) Cold-start fraction (requests served before full weight residency) drops below 5% for P1 tenants on a 10-minute ramp; 3) Memory overhead per node from KV Stabilizer cover remains <10% for standard configurations and <20% for premium tier; 4) Integration tests for admission controller soft-reservations, lease renewal, and eviction grace pass in CI; 5) Canary rollout shows no increase in 5xx rate for other tenants.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Prototype): implement slate format and minimal loader, basic KV prefill worker, and a kube-side autoscaler hook. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4382. Phase 2 (Hardening): integrate admission controller, implement soft-lease protocol, refine eviction heuristics, add metrics. Phase 3 (Rollout): small canary on dedicated-staging, expand to 10% prod traffic, then full rollout. Estimated engineering tasks: loader + RTC (3 days), kv stabilizer worker (5 days), autoscaler hook (2 days), tests + infra (5 days).
rollouts: Canary plan: start with dedicated-staging fleet (0.5% traffic), run 48h soak with synthetic ramps, then 10% customer traffic for 72h. Monitoring gates: no increase in 5xx, P95 latency improvement >=30% for canary tenants, memory pressure stable. Fallback: admission controller immediately disables seeding for flagged node pools and triggers graceful tear-down of seeded slates.
telemetry: Signals: P95 and P99 tail latency; cold-start fraction (requests served before full param residency); RAM and GPU memory utilization; kv-hit-rate for pre-filled prefixes; lease churn rate; autoscaler spin-ups attributable to seeding. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/dedicated-warmpool and incident dashboard link above. Alerts: P99 > 2x SLO or 'cold-start fraction' >10% for >15m.
comments: 2026-01-28 Maya Chen: Created ticket after post-incident review. Initial spec uploaded to Confluence and linked prototype PR opened.

2026-02-04 Liam O'Connor: Spike results - prototype reduced initial weight transfer time by 42% in lab tests; KV prefill increased cache hit-rate for synthetic prompt mixes by 28% but added ~6% memory overhead on m40 nodes.
2026-02-18 Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria; requested explicit per-tenant budget controls and a clear opt-in for Reserved customers. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-02-25 Carlos Martinez (SRE): Noted risk: slate streaming can exacerbate node-level CPU contention if staged concurrently with many tenants. Suggested staggered slot admission and rate-limit on local streaming I/O.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Implemented soft-lease protocol (draft) and pushed integration tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4510. Tests show lease renewal reduces eviction churn in prewarm nodes.
2026-03-08 QA: Load test run ID run-20260308-09 completed. Results uploaded to dashboard; meeting scheduled to review tuning knobs with PM and SRE.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Decision: proceed with phased rollout targeting runtime-1.20. Post-rollout tasks: add per-tenant prefill budget UI in Console (PM ticket pending) and a postmortem template to capture any anomalies.
